full_judgment:
The petitioner Major (Retd.) Rafiq Hasan Faruq, Managing Director of M/S Blue Bird Garments (Pvt.) Ltd., in course of his business, obtained some loan from respondent No.3, Sonali Bank, Ramna Corporate Branch, Dhaka (shortly the Bank) by mortgaging 24 decimals of land and structures thereon. But he failed to repay the loan. So, the Bank filed Artha Rin Suit No.491 of 2004 in the Artha Rin Adalat, 1st Court, Dhaka (shortly, the Adalat) for recovery of the loan with interest. Eventually, the suit was decreed exparte for an amount of Tk.5,40,49,309.76/. 

 3. The decree holder Bank initiated Artha Execution Case No.120 of 2005, which was dismissed due to default of the Bank to publish auction notices in two daily news papers. Thereafter the decree holder Bank instituted the present Artha Execution Case No.682 of 2005. 

 7. Mr. Md. Faruk flossain, the learned Advocate, appearing for the decree-holder Bank, with reference to the affidavit-in-opposition, submitted that the provision of Order 21 Rule 83 of the Code is not applicable in this case. 

 8. Mr. Faruk, the learned Advocate further submitted that the Ain, 2003 is a self contained law with adequate provisions for execution of a decree. He put emphasis on the fact that since petitioner has authorized the Bank by registered deed with irrevocable power of attorney to sell the mortgaged property as the security for repayment of the loan, the Adalat has no lawful authority to grant permission for selling the property by the petitioner by negotiation. 

 Mr. Sharif, the learned Advocate next submits that if the petitioner-company is allowed to sell the schedule property by private negotiation it will not affect the interest of the decree-holder Bank in any manner, but the petitioner will be benefited, because he can sell the property at a higher price than the one in an auction proceeding of a court and thus he gets an opportunity to discharge his liability to a greater extent. 

 "83.(1) Where an order for the sale of immovable property has been made, if the judgment-debtor can satisfy the Court that there is reason to believe that the amount of the decree may be raised by the mortgage or lease or private sale of such property, or some part thereof, or of any other immovable property of the judgment-debtor, the Court may, on his  application, postpone the sale of the property comprised in the order for sale  on such terms and for such period as it thinks proper, to enable him to raise the amount. 

 Provided that all monies payable under such mortgage, lease or sale shall be paid, not to the judgment - debtor. but save in so far as a decree-holder is entitled to set-off such money under the provision of rule 72, into Court: 

 (3) Nothing in this rule shall be deemed to apply to a sale of property directed to be sold in execution of a decree for sale in enforcement of a mortgage of or charge on, such property." 

 It is evident from plain reading of rule 83 that it contemplates a situation where an order for sale of a mortgage property has been passed but the sale has not taken place. In such situation the Judgment debtor may for satisfying the amount of the decree, take an opportunity to raise money by mortgage or lease or by private sale of the property. However, he has to obtain a certificate and in granting a certificate the court must be satisfied that such a course of action would be more advantageous than a Court sale. The 1st and 2nd proviso to sub-rule (2) also specify the procedure to be followed after granting of certificate. 

 14. The legislative intent of rule 83 is to facilitate, and not to obstruct, the satisfaction of the decree through private initiative of the judgment debtor instead of the court process. The rational is, such a course would not affect the interest of the decree holder, and rather it is likely to pave the way for better satisfaction of the amount of the decree. 

 15. In our view the expression "the amount" occurring in this rule means "the whole amount and no permission can be granted by the court unless the entire decreetal debt can be realized at the private initiative. 

 Section 26 of the Ain, 2003 provides for application of the Code of Civil Procedure in execution of a decree of an Artha Rin Adalat so far the relevant provision of the Code is not inconsistent with the provisions of the Ain. 

 17. We have also gone through the unreported decision of a Division Bench in the case of SDS Dairy Limited -Vs-Bangladesh and others. There are fundamental similarities between the facts of that case with those of the present case. It was decided in that case that, for satisfying the decree passed in a Artha Rin Suit, the judgment-debtor may be allowed by the Executing Court to undertake private initiative for selling a mortgage property and to deposit the sale proceeds or part there of within specified time to satisfy the decree. 

 18. It is to be noted that in the application filed in the Adalat and also in this Writ petition, the petitioner has expressed his intention to sell not only the mortgage property described in the scheduled of the application of the Execution Case but also other properties, for satisfying the decreetal dues. But since the other properties are not under order of sale in the Execution Case at this stage, certificate can not be granted by the Adalat under the said rule 83 in respect of other properties. However, the petitioner remains under the obligation: to deposit the entire dues. 

 21. The learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka being the concerned executing Court is directed to grant certificate under order XXI rule 83(2) of the Code allowing the petitioner to sell the schedule property of Artha Execution Case No.682 of 2009 within a time to be specified by the Adalat. If the petitioner fails to sell the property under sale by within the specific time and to deposit the requisite amount of money in the court for satisfying the decree within the specified time, the execution case will proceed in accordance with law.
